Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:10:1.english: Rav Yehuda proclaimed in Pumbedita - That was where he resided:

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:10:2.english: Balla’ai, Danna’ai, Talla’ai, Malla’ai, Zagga’ai - [These are] names of places or families.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:10:3.hebrew: גובאי - גבעוני. כלומר: על שם שהיו גבעונים, נקראו בבבל גובאי, קרוב לגבעונים בשמן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:10:3.english: Gova’ai - [They are] Gibeonites. That is to say: Because they were Gibeonites, they were called in Babylonia “Gova’ai,” [a name] close to “Gibeonites” in their name.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:10:4.hebrew: דורנונית דרא דנתינאי - כפר נתינים היה. דורא — כפר, כדאמר (עירובין דף ז:) "דורא דרעותא", "א"ל מרי דוראי" (פסחים דף כה:). ועל שם שהוא כפר נתיני, נקרא דורנינות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:10:4.english: Dorenunita [is] a village of Netinim - It was a village of Netinim. Dora [means] a village, as it says (Eruvin 7b): "Dora dera'avata" [a village of shepherds], [and] "He said to him: The master of my village [mari dora'i]" (Pesachim 25b). And because it was a village of Netinim, it was called Doreninot.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:10:5.hebrew: בי כובי דפומבדיתא - כפר הסמוך אל פומבדיתא, דמקרי בי כובי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:10:5.english: Bei Kuvei of Pumbedita - A village adjacent to Pumbedita that is called Bei Kuvei.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:11:1.english: Pashḥur ben Immer - He lived in the days of Jeremiah.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:11:2.hebrew: וכולן נטמעו בכהונה - ול"ג גדולה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:11:2.english: And all of them were assimilated into the priesthood - And we do not read "great" [i.e., the High Priesthood].

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:11:3.hebrew: נטמעו - נדמעו. נשאו בנות כהנים, שהיו מחזיקין עצמן בכהנים, מתוך שהיו אוכלים תרומה מחמת [שהיו] עבדי כהנים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:11:3.english: They were assimilated - They became intermingled. They married daughters of priests, for they held themselves out as priests, since they would eat terumah because [they were] slaves of priests.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:11:4.hebrew: אל תהרהר אחריו - אחר משפחתם, שהם בני מריבה, כדכתיב: ״כמריבי כהן״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:11:4.english: Do not speculate about him - [Do not cast doubt] on their family [lineage], for they are contentious people, as it is written: “Like those who strive with a priest” [Hosea 4:4].

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:12:1.hebrew: עדות לישראל - אותן שהן ישראל, הוא מעיד עליהן שהן משלו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:12:1.english: A testimony to Israel - [Concerning] those who are Israel, He testifies about them that they are His.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:13:1.english: Families of Israel - Families that are pure Israelites.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:14:1.hebrew: בישראל כתיב - ״והייתי להם לאלהים״ — אע"פ שאינם לי לעם, ומתוך שאני מקרבן, ״הם יהיו לי לעם״. אבל גרים — אין מקרבין אותן מן השמים, אלא אם כן הן מקרבין עצמם תחילה להיות טובים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:14:1.english: With regard to Israel it is written - “And I will be their God” — even though they are not [yet] My people; and because I draw them close, “they shall be My people.” But converts — they are not drawn close from Heaven unless they first draw themselves close, to be good.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:15:1.hebrew: קשין גרים - שאינם זהירים במצות, והרגילים אצלם נמשכים אצלם ולומדים מן מעשיהם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:15:1.english: Converts are difficult - For they are not meticulous with the mitzvot, and those who associate with them are drawn to them and learn from their deeds.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:1:1.hebrew: אין שואלין בשלום אשה - שמא מתוך שאילת שלום יהיו רגילים זה עם זה ע"י שלוחם, ויבואו לידי חיבה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:1:1.english: One may not inquire after the welfare of a woman - Lest through inquiring after [her] welfare they become familiar with one another through their messenger, and come to affection.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:1:2.hebrew: אמר ליה רב נחמן ע"י בעלה - אהיה אני שליח לדבר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:1:2.english: Rav Naḥman said to him: Through her husband - I will be the messenger for the matter.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:1:3.english: One may not inquire after the welfare of a woman at all - For it familiarizes her heart and mind with him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:1:4.english: She sent to him - Yalta [sent] to Rav Naḥman.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:1:5.hebrew: שרי ליה תיגריה - פטור אותו מלפניך. זה לשון הגמרא לומר מישרי ליה תיגריה, כשממהר לעשות בקשת האיש או דינו, כדי להפטר ממנו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:1:5.english: Release his dispute for him - Dismiss him from before you. This is the phrasing of the Gemara to say "to release his dispute," when one hastens to carry out a person's request or his legal case, in order to be rid of him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:2:1.hebrew: מאי שיאטיה דמר הכא - מה דרכו של אדוני לשוט הלום? כלומר: למה בא אדוני הנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:2:1.english: What is the Master’s roaming here - What is my master’s way to wander hither? That is to say: Why did my master come here?

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:2:2.english: I do not know the Master’s speech - I do not understand the speech of my master, [so as] to speak with the elegance of his language.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:2:3.english: I would summon him to court - [This is said] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:2:4.hebrew: אפיק דיסקא דאזמנותא - הוציא שטר הזמנה מחיקו, ששלח לו רב נחמן שיבא לפניו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:2:4.english: He took out the document of summons - He took out from his bosom the document of summons that Rav Naḥman had sent him, to come before him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:2:5.english: From his chest - From within his bosom.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:2:6.english: Let the Master speak his words - Let him state his defense regarding his dispute with that man.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:3:1.hebrew: ציער שליחא דרבנן - ביזה את שלוחו לפניו, וחייב מלקות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:3:1.english: He caused distress to an agent of the Sages - He degraded his agent in his presence, and he is liable to lashes.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:3:2.hebrew: דרב מנגיד אמאן דמצער שליח דרבנן - כדאמר בפ' קמא (לעיל קידושין דף יב:):
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:3:2.english: As Rav would flog one who causes discomfort to an agent of the Sages - As [the Gemara] states in the first chapter (above, Kiddushin 12b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:3:3.english: That which is greater than it - [A punishment] more severe than it I did to him to penalize him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:5:1.hebrew: אדהכי אמר ההוא בר דיניה לרב יהודה לדידי - דאתינא מבית חשמונאי, קרית לי עבד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:5:1.english: Meanwhile, that litigant said to Rav Yehuda: To me - [Me,] who descend from the house of the Hasmoneans, did you call a slave?!

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:5:2.hebrew: כל דאמר מבית חשמונאי אנא עבד הוא - שכל זרעו הרגם הורדוס, ועבד היה ומלך תחתיהן, וקרא בניו על שם בית חשמונאי. ומסתמא לאו בנות ישראל נסיב, דנזהרים הם להשיא בנותם לעבדים, והוו להו כולם עבדים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:5:2.english: Anyone who says: “I am from the house of the Hasmoneans,” is a slave - For Herod killed all of their descendants, and he was a slave and reigned in their place, and called his sons after the house of the Hasmoneans. And presumably he did not marry daughters of Israel, for they are careful [not] to marry off their daughters to slaves, and [so] they all became slaves:

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:6:1.hebrew: אם קודם שבא מעשה לידו אמרה - להאי שמועה לתלמידיו בשם רבו, נאמן לאומרה בשעת מעשה. ואם לאו, אינו נאמן להעיד בשם רבו, שמא מחמת מעשה הבא לידו הוא אמר כן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:6:1.english: If he stated it before an incident came to his hand - [If he stated] this tradition to his students in the name of his teacher, he is trusted to state it at the time of the incident. And if not, he is not trusted to testify in the name of his teacher, lest he said so on account of the incident that came to his hand.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:7:1.english: On the bank - The bank of the river.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:7:2.hebrew: אמברא - על הגשר, אי נמי: בתוך הספינה לעבור הנהר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:7:2.english: On the ferry - On the bridge; alternatively, inside the boat [used] to cross the river.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:7:3.hebrew: כל דאמר מבית חשמונאי אנא עבד הוא - שכל זרעו הרגם הורדוס, ועבד היה ומלך תחתיהן, וקרא בניו על שם בית חשמונאי. ומסתמא לאו בנות ישראל נסיב, דנזהרים הם להשיא בנותם לעבדים, והוו להו כולם עבדים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:7:3.english: Anyone who says, "I am from the house of the Hasmoneans," is a slave - For Herod killed all of his [Hasmonean's] descendants; and he was a slave and reigned in their stead, and he called his sons after the name of the house of the Hasmoneans. And presumably, he did not marry daughters of Israel, as they are careful not to give their daughters in marriage to slaves, and [so] they all became slaves.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:9:1.hebrew: איקרע' כמה כתובתא - מנשי אותה המשפחה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:9:1.english: Several marriage contracts were torn up - From the women of that family.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:9:2.english: When he was leaving - Rav Yehuda.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:9:3.english: To stone him - Because he revealed their flawed lineage.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:9:5.hebrew: וקם אטמא בנהר מלכא - באותן האבנים שהשליכום בנהר, עמד מכשול סתימה במי הנהר ומנע את מהלך המים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:9:5.english: And a dam arose in the Malka River - From those stones that they threw into the river, an obstructive blockage arose in the water of the river and prevented the flow of the water.

Rashi on Kiddushin 70b:9:6.english: A dam - A blockage, as [the Targum] translates [the Hebrew word] "they stopped them up" [satmum] as "they plugged them" [temunun] (Genesis 26).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 70b:15:1.hebrew: קשים גרים - פי' בקונטרס: לפי שאינם בקיאים במצות ומביאים פורענות, ועוד שמלמדים את ישראל ממעשיהם, וכו'. וי"מ: לפי שכל ישראל ערבין זה בזה. ולאו מילתא היא, דהא לא נתערבו בשביל הגרים כשקבלו התורה, כדאמרינן בסוטה (דף לז:): נמצא לכל אחד מישראל שש מאות אלף וג' אלפים [ותק"ן בריתות], שכולן נתערבו זה בזה; אלמא לא נתערבו מן הגרים, שהרי הרבה ערב רב עלה אתם. ויש מפרשים, דקשין גרים לישראל כספחת לפי שהזהיר הקב"ה עליהם בכ"ד מקומות שלא להונות אותם, ואי אפשר שלא יצערום. ויש מפרשים, לפי שע"י הגרים ישראל בגלות, כדאמר (פסחים דף פז:): מפני מה ישראל מפוזרים בכל ארצות יותר משאר עובדי כוכבים? כדי שיתוספו עליהם גרים. ולא נהירא, דהא אמר ביבמות (דף מז.): עובד כוכבים הבא להתגייר אומרים לו: מה ראית שבאת להתגייר? תדע שישראל דווים דחופים... ואמרי' התם: משום דיפרוש, הוא דאמר מר קשין גרים לישראל כספחת — אלמא דבתר שיתגיירו קשים הם. וה"ר אברהם גר פירש: לפי שהגרין בקיאין במצות ומדקדקין בהם, קשים הם לישראל כספחת, דמתוך כן הקב"ה מזכיר עונותיהם של ישראל כשאין עושין רצונו. וכה"ג מצינו גבי הצרפית (מלכים א יז) שאמרה: "מה לי ולך איש האלהים, (כי) באת אלי להזכיר [את] עוני" — שמתוך שהוא צדיק גמור, היה נראה לה שמזכיר השם עונה. ור"י פירש, דלפיכך קשים: שנטמעו בישראל, ואין השכינה שורה אלא על משפחה מיוחסת. וכן נראה, דמשום הכי מייתי הא דרבי חלבו על הא מילתא דר' חמא בר חנינא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 70b:15:1.english: Converts are difficult - [Rashi] explained in the commentary: Because they are not proficient in the mitzvot and bring retribution, and furthermore because they teach Israel from their deeds, etc. And some explain: Because all of Israel are guarantors for one another. But this is not correct, for they did not become guarantors for converts when they received the Torah, as we say in Sotah (37b): "It turns out that for each and every one of Israel there were 600,000 and 3,000 [and 550 covenants] that all became guarantors for one another"; evidently, they did not become guarantors for the converts, for a great mixed multitude went up with them. And some explain that converts are as difficult for Israel as a scab because the Holy One, Blessed be He, warned concerning them in twenty-four places not to mistreat them, and it is impossible not to cause them distress. And some explain: Because through the converts Israel is in exile, as it says (Pesachim 87b): "Why are Israel scattered throughout all the lands more than the other nations? In order that converts may be added to them." But this is not clear, for it says in Yevamot (47a): "A gentile who comes to convert, we say to him: 'What did you see that caused you to come to convert? Do you not know that Israel are anguished and downtrodden...?'" And we say there: [This is] so that he might withdraw, for the Master said: "Converts are as difficult for Israel as a scab" — evidently, after they convert they are difficult. And the Rabbi, R. Abraham the Convert, explained: Because converts are proficient in the mitzvot and scrupulous with them, they are as difficult for Israel as a scab, for because of this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, recalls the iniquities of Israel when they do not perform His will. And we find similarly regarding the woman of Zarephath (I Kings 17), who said: "What have I to do with you, O man of God? Have you come to me to recall my iniquity?" — for because he was completely righteous, it appeared to her that God was recalling her iniquity. And the Ri explained that they are difficult for this reason: because they assimilate into Israel, whereas the Divine Presence rests only upon a family of pure lineage. And so it appears, for it is because of this that [the Gemara] brings this [statement] of Rabbi Chelbo regarding that statement of Rabbi Chama bar Chanina.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 70b:1:1.hebrew: אין שואלין בשלום אשה כלל - והא דאמר בהשוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ דף פז.): "איה שרה אשתך", ששואלין בשלום האשה על ידי בעלה — היינו דוקא בשאילת שלום; אבל לשלוח לה בשלום, אפילו ע"י בעלה — אסור:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 70b:1:1.english: "One may not inquire after the welfare of a woman at all" - And that which [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] HaSokher Et HaPoalim (Bava Metzia 87a) regarding "Where is Sarah your wife?" — that one may inquire after the welfare of a woman through her husband — that is specifically inquiring after [her] welfare; but sending greetings to her, even through her husband, is forbidden.
